Let <MATH_0001> be a left adjoint to <MATH_0002> as in Definition <REF_0001>.
Then
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0003> is fully faithful <MATH_0004> <MATH_0005>
<MATH_0006> <MATH_0007> is an isomorphism,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0008> is fully faithful <MATH_0009>
<MATH_0010> <MATH_0011>
<MATH_0012> is an isomorphism.
<STRUCT_0004>

Proof of (1).
Assume <MATH_0001> is fully faithful. We will show <MATH_0002>
is an isomorphism. Let <MATH_0003> be any morphism.
By adjointness this corresponds to a morphism <MATH_0004>. By fully
faithfulness of <MATH_0005> this corresponds to a unique morphism <MATH_0006>.
Thus we see that post-composing by <MATH_0007> defines a bijection
<MATH_0008>. Hence <MATH_0009> is an isomorphism.
If there exists an isomorphism <MATH_0010> of functors,
then <MATH_0011> is fully faithful. By
Lemma <REF_0001> we see
that <MATH_0012> is fully faithful. By the above this implies <MATH_0013>
is an isomorphism. Thus all <MATH_0014> conditions are equivalent (and these
conditions are also equivalent to <MATH_0015> being fully faithful).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Part (2) is dual to part (1).
